recommendation: Build Kadıköy as a separate street layer. An offline compiler, written in Node and reusing Evren's OSM and façade code, will emit plain glTF files plus JSON manifests that any engine can load; Blender does the baking. Choose the runtime from measured results, not from how much code carries over: compile one ~200 m strip from the Rıhtım into the çarşı, then render the same files in three.js r186 WebGPURenderer and in Godot 4.7 Forward+, next to Blender reference renders, and hold both to one hard street-level test (day, dusk and night with 32 lights, 200 animated people, an open café door, a walking camera, 60 fps). Rule out three.js's current WebGL2 renderer for street level: its missing features are confirmed in node_modules/three. Whichever runtime passes carries the game forward. If both pass, three.js WebGPU wins the tie because it keeps the web link and the flight game. If only Godot passes, the walking game moves to Godot on desktop and the current flight demo stays live on the web as a teaser.
why:
Street-level detail depends mostly on the content and on splitting the world into layers; the engine matters less. Shipped games separate their flight or driving scale from their street scale:
- Starfield treats space and planet surface as two 'realities'.
- Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom starts loading when you approach an entrance.
- Spider-Man's city was generated procedurally, then polished by hand, and its room interiors are faked.
- Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 shows what happens without the split: its photogrammetry is meant to look convincing from the air, not at street level.

The compiler, the Kadıköy kit and the strip are therefore needed in every runtime, which makes them safe to start now.

Three.js r186 on WebGL2 cannot light or smooth a street at eye level without building it all ourselves. I checked this in node_modules/three 0.186.0:
- TAARenderPass accumulates frames only while nothing moves (it has no reprojection).
- GTAOPass and SSRPass draw the whole scene a second time.
- LightProbeGridWebGL gives diffuse light only and picks one grid per object.
- The WebGL renderer has no clustered lights and no local reflection probes, and adding or removing a light recompiles shaders.

Three.js does have the equivalents, but only for WebGPU: tsl/display/TRAANode, GTAONode, SSRNode, SSGINode, plus lighting/ClusteredLighting, DynamicLighting and LightProbeGrid.

The two credible runtimes are close, and switching between them later would be costly, so it is worth measuring rather than guessing.
- Three.js WebGPU keeps the web link and most of the 113k lines. Its price: porting about 12.6k lines of GLSL (31 ShaderMaterials, 5 onBeforeCompile patches, and the global atmosphere hook in uniforms.ts) to TSL on a renderer the manual still calls experimental, and building every gameplay system ourselves.
- Godot 4.7 Forward+ has most of this built in: 512 clustered lights, ReflectionProbe, SSR/SSAO/SSIL, SDFGI and LightmapGI, TAA/FSR2, decals, occlusion culling, visibility ranges, automatic LOD, Jolt physics, navigation, AnimationTree/IK, text scene files and an editor whose viewport is the real renderer. Its price: its web export only supports the WebGL2 compatibility renderer, and the flight game would have to be rebuilt.
- The engine research scored them 3.81 and 3.56.

One comparison on content we need anyway is cheaper than an irreversible guess. A Blender render of the same tile shows what the content itself can look like, so a content failure is not mistaken for a renderer failure.

Count the new work needed for the walking slice, not the lines kept.
- The same on both paths: the compiler, the kit, the interiors, the ink story, the NPC writing and the save format. That is the real bottleneck.
- Built in on Godot but built by us on three.js: character controller, navigation and avoidance, the animation state machine, instanced animated crowds, occlusion culling and HLOD, reflection probes, the lighting-bake pipeline, TAA, and input contexts.
- Most of the code that three.js keeps is flight and far-field code that the street goal barely reuses.

The shared compiler output has to be plain glTF. Godot's importer refuses files that list EXT_meshopt_compression or KHR_mesh_quantization as required extensions; I checked godotengine master: modules/gltf/extensions has only KTX, WebP, light and spec-gloss handlers, and gltf_document.cpp:7414 errors out on unsupported required extensions. So we compile once to plain glTF and package separately for each runtime.

Kadıköy's core is built for walking. The repo's own research (.docs/research/kadikoy-hero-spots.json) describes the market as a grid of 4–8 m pedestrian lanes, and Bahariye as a 723 m pedestrian street carrying the tram. The first slice is therefore walk, enter and talk. Driving comes later, on the real car streets: Rıhtım Cd and Söğütlüçeşme Cd.
rejected: Keeping three.js WebGL2 r186 for the street layer (the draft's plan): the gaps checked above (no reprojection TAA, second scene pass for AO and reflections, per-object diffuse probes, no clustered lights or local reflection probes) mean either building each one ourselves on a renderer that will get 'no larger new features', or accepting a weak night street.

Committing to Godot now, with no comparison: it will probably win on fidelity, but the move is irreversible, costs the flight game and the web link, and a 1–2 session comparison on content we need anyway is cheaper.

The critique's version of the comparison, with WebGL instead of WebGPU as three.js's entrant: WebGL's gaps are already confirmed, so the comparison would only restate them. WebGPU is the best the browser can do, and that is what needs testing.

Unreal 5.8: its assets and levels are binary files, its MCP plugin is experimental and editor-only, Epic recommends an M3 (the M2 Max falls short), Nanite and virtual shadow maps are beta on Mac, there is no web export, and UE6/Verse is coming.

Unity 6.6 on WebGPU, the only engine switch that keeps a browser build: according to the 6.6 docs its web build has baked GI only, non-directional lightmaps only, and no dynamic resolution on WebGPU. It also has agent friction: scene files are YAML linked by GUIDs, the editor locks the project against batch runs, and the official MCP is paid on the Personal plan. Three.js WebGPU is the stronger web option.
Bevy 0.19: no editor, IK, navmesh, terrain or streaming, and the API breaks every 5–6 months.
Walking on the existing flight world everywhere, as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 does: façades built for 50–500 m look wrong from 1.7 m, and the OSM slice is already 31–46 M triangles.
Photogrammetry or Google 3D Tiles: the licence forbids caching, the lighting is baked in (breaking day/night and interiors), and the meshes are not walkable.
Generating street detail at runtime: it cannot be art-directed and it costs frame time. Bake it offline, then polish it.

A separate façade kit modelled in Blender: it would duplicate the existing TypeScript detail generators (src/world/osm/buildings/props.ts, signs.ts). Run those in Node instead, and use Blender only for bakes, reference renders and hand-made hero pieces.
three-fenestra: it is GLSL injected through onBeforeCompile and duplicates fRoom/fShop in facade-glsl.ts. Port those two to TSL or Godot's shader language instead.

Light-probe grids per tile, baked when the tile loads: each probe takes six scene renders, which would cause hitches. Bake offline at 4 times of day and blend between them; re-bake at runtime only inside small interiors.
Driving in the first milestone: the çarşı and Bahariye are pedestrian. Driving becomes phase 7, on Rıhtım Cd and Söğütlüçeşme Cd.
A seamless first café: a fixed shell will not fit arbitrary OSM footprints. Start with parametric shells and a short fade at the door; go seamless after one fitted example passes the test.
Running the test on a mid-range integrated-GPU machine (critique): only the M2 Max is available. Use a 'medium' preset at 1280×720 as a stand-in, and state that the target is desktop-class GPUs.
Feeding GTAOPass the depth buffer via setGBuffer (critique): no longer relevant, because WebGL2 post-processing passes are not used for the street.

LLM-driven NPCs as the dialogue foundation: roughly $0.01–0.20 per player-hour on a free demo, easy to exploit (Where Winds Meet players did), and Chrome's built-in Gemini Nano does not support Turkish.
keepChangeStop:
KEEP
- The live three.js flight game and web demo, the engine skeleton (systems, services, events, workers) and the tsc + snap.mjs loop. The flight demo stays live in every outcome, either as the base game or as the web teaser.
- The phase-01 fixes already running: let them finish, since they improve the live demo, but add no new walking-related work to 01-A. Phase 01-B stays limited to bugs and performance, with no near-field polish in Kadıköy.
- The Galata OSM slice: frozen behind ?osm=1. Its generators become compiler inputs: props.ts, signs.ts, StreetSurface, furniture, the crowd walk graph and the IDM traffic simulation.
- The Kadıköy hero-spot research becomes the hero list:
  - built at walking scale: both piers, Haldun Taner, İskele Camii, Şehremaneti, Osmanağa, Surp Takavor, the Boğa statue, Süreyya and Bahariye;
  - left as flight-scale landmarks: Şükrü Saracoğlu, the marina, the lighthouse and the parks.

CHANGE
- src/world/osm/area.ts: from one Galata bounding box to a list of areas, each with its own data file and exclusion rectangle; also fetch entrance=*.
- Build Kadıköy once, at walking scale. Its low-detail tiles serve the view from the air, so there is no separate flight-scale Kadıköy pass.
- OSM buildings: from one merged mesh with one oriented box each to compiler-made tiles with building IDs, LOD, true-footprint colliders and doorways.
- Phase-10 rider: becomes a CC0 human (Quaternius now, MPFB2 later). Remove Mixamo from the README asset table: its FAQ forbids distributing the raw files, which a public MIT repo would do.
- Roadmap:
  - insert phases 0–2 (data and compiler, one strip, the runtime comparison) right after 01;
  - move 08/09 tiling and the landing pads behind the runtime decision;
  - move driving after walk, enter and talk.

STOP
- New GLSL or onBeforeCompile work, and WebGL2 post-processing passes (GTAOPass, SSRPass, TAARenderPass), for street content.
- Adding detail to the flight-scale slice, or rolling it out city-wide, before L1 tiling exists.
- Runtime generation of anything seen at eye level.
- Porting the flight world to TSL/WebGPU before the comparison picks the web.
- 01-A rider-face work.
- Phases 11, 12 and 14–15, parked until the Kadıköy slice ships.
- LLM NPCs, real brand names or logos, walking the whole city, and committing compiled binaries to git.

phases.name: 0 · Kadıköy data and compiler skeleton
phases.goal:
Make the OSM pipeline handle several areas and set up the offline compiler.
- area.ts becomes a list of areas; fetch Kadıköy, including entrance=*.
- Build Kadıköy's street surfaces, walk graph and lane graph in Node. The heavy slice layers do not run in Kadıköy at runtime; they only feed the compiler.
- The compiler writes plain glTF plus JSON manifests for each ~100 m tile, packages them for the web, and publishes them outside git.
- Add walk-test.mjs (fixed camera paths at 1.7 m eye height) and median/p99 frame times in snap.mjs.
phases.deliverable: Greybox Kadıköy tiles (true-footprint blocks with doorways, sidewalks and kerbs, a manifest of POIs and entrances), walked by a scripted eye-level camera on a three.js sandbox page, with a frame-time report.

phases.name: 1 · One Kadıköy strip (content only)
phases.goal:
Build the ~200 m strip from the Rıhtım into the çarşı at walking scale. No character or physics yet.
- Façade kit for the dominant balconied apartment type of the 1950s–70s, generated by the existing detail code run in Node, with real depth and openings. The historic pier is modelled by hand in Blender.
- Shopfronts placed from POIs, with fictional Turkish signs; cobbles, kerbs and street furniture; at least 32 lamp and sign lights for night.
- Blender AO bakes; offline probe and lightmap bakes at 4 times of day.
- 200 CC0 Quaternius pedestrians on the walk graph, plus one stand-in NPC.
- A greybox café interior behind an open door.
- Blender renders from 10 fixed cameras, each paired with a reference photo.
phases.deliverable: A content board of 10 Blender shots paired with reference photos (day, dusk, night) that pass the content checklist, with one revision round for the kit if they fail.

phases.name: 2 · Runtime comparison (go/no-go)
phases.goal: Render the identical packaged strip in three.js r186 WebGPURenderer (a sandbox page) and in Godot 4.7 Forward+, with the same cameras, the same walking path and the same test. Choose the runtime by the fixed rule in the first-milestone section.
phases.deliverable: A side-by-side board: 10 shots in each runtime next to the Blender version, walking frame sequences, a performance table ('high' preset at 1600×900 and 'medium' at 1280×720), and how long an agent takes to make one look change. The decision is recorded.

phases.name: 3 · Walk
phases.deliverable: Step off the ferry and walk, jog and run over kerbs and steps through the strip and the greybox around it. Reloading puts you back on the same spot. walk-test passes.

phases.name: 4 · Step inside and talk
phases.goal:
- A parametric café shell fitted to its OSM building, entered through a short fade at the door.
- The ink runtime with external functions, tags and Ink-Localiser.
- One hero NPC with a navigation agent, turning to face you, and a two-shot dialogue camera.
- Rule-matched barks from passers-by.
- Save v1 including the ink state.
- Scripted interaction checks in walk-test: door opened, seated, flag set, save round-trip.
phases.deliverable: Walk into the café, sit, and order çay in a Turkish ink conversation whose choice sets a flag. A passer-by comments outside. Save, reload, and both are kept.

phases.name: 5 · The heart of Kadıköy
phases.goal:
Widen the street layer to about 0.4 km²: Rıhtım, çarşı, Altıyol, and Bahariye up to Süreyya.
- Two more façade types, plus corner and pasaj pieces.
- Hero spots at walking scale.
- The nostalgic tram on Bahariye.
- 5 enterable places built from 3 shells.
- 8–10 hero NPCs with daily schedules.
- A full night pass.
phases.deliverable: A 20–30 minute walk-and-talk loop, by day and by night, that still passes the phase-2 test.

phases.name: 6 · From sky to street
phases.goal:
Bring flight and street together in one runtime.
- On three.js: port the flight world's GLSL (about 12.6k lines, 31 ShaderMaterials, 5 onBeforeCompile patches and the atmosphere hook) to TSL.
- On Godot: rebuild terrain, sea, sky and clouds; export the dragon rig once to glTF and port the flight code.
- On both: L1 OSM tiles, 2–3 landing pads (Rıhtım, Moda Burnu) that preload as you approach, and dismounting by a cut plus a UAL clip.
phases.deliverable: Fly from Galata to Kadıköy, land on a pad, and be walking within 3 s with no hitch over 50 ms. The Galata slice fits the flight budget.
phases.effort: L×3–4 (the largest phase on either path)

phases.name: 7 · Drive
phases.goal:
- A raycast vehicle: get in and out, a chase camera, and a parked car that becomes drivable.
- The player's car joins the IDM traffic simulation as a leader, on Kadıköy's real car streets (Rıhtım Cd towards Haydarpaşa, and Söğütlüçeşme Cd).
phases.deliverable: Take a parked taxi on Rıhtım Cd, drive a loop while AI traffic yields, park, and walk into the çarşı.

phases.name: 8 · Chapter one
phases.goal: A quest journal and 3–5 ink quests that mix flying, walking and driving. Galata–Karaköy becomes the second street district, reusing the kits.
phases.deliverable: A playable first chapter of 1–2 hours across the sky and Kadıköy's streets.

risks: The comparison adds about one session and may end close. The tie rule handles that: three.js by default, Godot only if you see a clear quality difference.

Either winner brings a big port later, in phase 6.
- Web: moving the flight game to WebGPU means rewriting about 12.6k lines of GLSL into TSL, on a renderer the three.js manual still calls experimental.
- Godot: rebuilding the flight game takes months, the traffic and crowd simulations must be ported, and the full-quality web link is lost (Godot's web export is WebGL2 compatibility only).

Checking the work gets harder on both sides.
- Headless Chrome hides WebGPU unless it is launched with WebGPU enabled, and otherwise quietly tests the WebGL2 fallback.
- Godot's --headless mode renders nothing, so captures need a real window on the shared Mac, queued like snap.mjs.
Godot on Apple Silicon: whether SDFGI, LightmapGI baking and TAA behave well on this Mac's graphics backend has to be proven in phase 2, not assumed.

The content could look procedural: repetitive and too clean. The Blender reference render catches this before any engine is blamed. The fixes: typologies built from photo references, per-building variation from OSM data, weathering decals, hand-made hero buildings, and your sign-off on runtime renders.

Characters: there is no motion matching and no facial animation, and Quaternius's semi-stylised humans may clash with a realistic street. Keep NPCs at medium framing, offer a first-person view, and bring in MPFB2 for hero NPCs later.
Content volume: every interior and hero NPC has to be dressed, written and staged. The caps (3–4 shells; 5–10 interiors and 8–10 hero NPCs per district) must hold.

Lighting bakes and download size: probe and lightmap bakes run offline at a few times of day, and only small interiors are re-baked at runtime. Tiles are kept out of git and hosted in releases or on R2, to stay under the 1 GB GitHub Pages limit and the recommended repo size.
decisionsForUser: Web or desktop: is a desktop download acceptable for the walking game, with the current flight demo kept on the web as a teaser? If the browser must carry the whole game, Godot drops out of the comparison, and a failed test means cutting scope, not switching engines. I recommend allowing desktop.

The look at street level: I recommend grounded realism (real proportions, CC0 photo-scanned materials, CC0 humans kept at medium framing). Nothing in the browser has proven this look yet, so you judge it on runtime renders in phase 2.
Walkable area: first the ~200 m strip from the Rıhtım into the çarşı. Then about 0.4 km²: Rıhtım → çarşı → Altıyol (Boğa) → Bahariye up to Süreyya. Moda comes later.
Story: the premise and tone, Turkish first with English, real streets and landmarks named, all businesses fictional.
